THOUGHT: The patient is an older, photodamaged white woman with prior nonmelanoma skin cancer who developed eruptive, firm verrucoid keratotic papules on the face two weeks after fractional CO2 resurfacing and fat transfer. The timing after procedure suggests Koebnerization/trauma-induced emergence of preexisting photodamaged lesions. Histology shows an atypical squamous proliferation with mature, hypergranulotic/keratinizing cells and keratin-filled cysts; a second biopsy specifically confirmed verrucous actinic keratosis. These clinical and pathologic features point to actinic keratoses of a verrucous/hypertrophic subtype as the leading diagnosis. Important differentials that can mimic this presentation include well‑differentiated squamous cell carcinoma (including verrucous carcinoma), HPV-related verruca (verruca vulgaris), and reactive pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia after trauma or laser. Seborrheic keratoses/irritated SKs are less likely given the biopsy findings.

DIAGNOSIS:
1) Verrucous actinic keratosis (most likely — consistent with clinical appearance, photodamage history, and biopsy confirmation)
2) Hypertrophic/vegetating actinic keratoses (closely related variant; clinical overlap with verrucous AK)
3) Well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma / verrucous squamous cell carcinoma (important to consider because AK can progress to SCC and histology can be difficult to distinguish)
4) Viral verruca (verruca vulgaris) — clinically similar and can arise in traumatized skin, though histology usually shows viral changes absent here
5) Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia / reactive epidermal hyperplasia from trauma or laser (can mimic atypical squamous proliferation clinically and histologically but usually lacks true cytologic atypia seen in AK/SCC)
